npcx: system: Fixed bug that ec received unexpected rtc interrupt In old system driver, ec clears "Predefined Time Occurred" (PTO) flag before setting a new alarm (PT field in WTC). If PT field is the same as the first 25 TTC bits at this moment, we might receive unexpected rtc interrupt again. This CL sets new alarm first then clears PTO flag to make sure rtc interrupt is issued from new alarm. HACK: CHROMIUM: temporarily slow down the NMI watchdog On some systems the turbo frequency can go higher than 5/2 times the TSC_MHz. This makes this timer tick too fast and trigger spurious hard LOCKUPs. Slow it down by a factor of 3 as a temporary workaround until it is switched a constant perf counter upstream. See also CL:502789 BUG=b:35587084 TEST=# This issue has been difficult to reproduce so first find a system # that is actually affected. To make sure it is, run: echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/watchdog_thresh turbostat --debug --interval=1 while true; do taskset -c 1 dd </dev/urandom >/dev/null 2>&1 \ bs=10M count=20; sleep 6; done & # The system is affected if Avg_MHz can go higher than 5/2 times # TSC_MHz. It will reboot and a spurious hard LOCKUP will be found # in /dev/pstore/console-ramoops. Try different taskset -c arguments. # Remove any intel_idle.max_cstate from the boot parameters. # Then apply this patch and stress the system again. Change-Id: I005574d4d5bd1f71e535616d61f9180680a161c5 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/506327 Commit-Ready: Marc Herbert <marc.herbert@intel.com> Tested-by: Casey G Bowman <casey.g.bowman@intel.com> Tested-by: Todd Broch <tbroch@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Todd Broch <tbroch@chromium.org>
